title: From X-ray to pixel: inside a digital sensor
topic: How a digital intraoral sensor turns X-ray photons into gray-level pixels, layer by layer, and how a PSP plate does it differently.

claims.claim: Layer stack of a solid-state sensor: housing, scintillator, fiber-optic plate, CMOS chip, read-out electronics + ADC (schematic model of one sensor design, not to scale)
claims.source: White & Pharoah, Oral Radiology: Principles and Interpretation, 7th ed. 2014, Ch. 4 Digital Imaging (Ludlow & Mol) - textbook, read in an online reproduction (printed page not seen), Fig. 4-3 caption (manufacturer-supplied figure). Not every sensor has a fiber-optic plate

claims.claim: Scintillator: X-ray -> visible light; CsI or Gd oxysulfide
claims.source: White & Pharoah, Oral Radiology: Principles and Interpretation, 7th ed. 2014, Ch. 4 Digital Imaging (Ludlow & Mol) - textbook, read in an online reproduction (printed page not seen); materials: Farman TT et al., Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol Endod 2005;99:608-13 (PMID 15829886), abstract

claims.claim: Fiber-optic plate: guides light, less noise
claims.source: White & Pharoah, Oral Radiology: Principles and Interpretation, 7th ed. 2014, Ch. 4 Digital Imaging (Ludlow & Mol) - textbook, read in an online reproduction (printed page not seen), Fig. 4-3 / 4-4 captions (couples the scintillator to the chip 'to reduce image noise'); textbook wording from a manufacturer figure, no PubMed-indexed dental measurement found

claims.claim: CMOS chip: light -> charge; a transistor at every pixel
claims.source: White & Pharoah, Oral Radiology: Principles and Interpretation, 7th ed. 2014, Ch. 4 Digital Imaging (Ludlow & Mol) - textbook, read in an online reproduction (printed page not seen) ('charge in each pixel proportional to the exposure'; 'each pixel is... directly connected to a transistor'); physics support: Arvanitis et al., Med Phys 2007;34:4612-25 (PMID 18196789), abstract

White & Pharoah, Oral Radiology: Principles and Interpretation, 7th ed. 2014, Ch. 4 Digital Imaging (Ludlow & Mol) - textbook, read in an online reproduction (printed page not seen) (analog-to-digital conversion; detectors capture 8, 10, 12 or 16 bits)

claims.claim: Image: number -> gray level. Toy model / schematic: 36 x 27 charge wells and a procedurally drawn periapical; more exposure = fuller well = darker pixel; well heights and the row-by-row build-up are illustrative
claims.source: White & Pharoah, Oral Radiology: Principles and Interpretation, 7th ed. 2014, Ch. 4 Digital Imaging (Ludlow & Mol) - textbook, read in an online reproduction (printed page not seen) (charge packets proportional to exposure; display convention); no measured values shown

claims.claim: PSP plate (Eu-doped barium fluorohalide): X-rays -> trapped electrons
claims.source: White & Pharoah, Oral Radiology: Principles and Interpretation, 7th ed. 2014, Ch. 4 Digital Imaging (Ludlow & Mol) - textbook, read in an online reproduction (printed page not seen); Leblans et al., Materials (Basel) 2011;4:1034-86 (PMID 28879966), PMC full text (medical computed-radiography review)

claims.claim: Red laser -> blue-violet light -> photomultiplier (schematic scanner)
claims.source: Leblans et al., Materials (Basel) 2011;4:1034-86 (PMID 28879966), PMC full text; White & Pharoah, Oral Radiology: Principles and Interpretation, 7th ed. 2014, Ch. 4 Digital Imaging (Ludlow & Mol) - textbook, read in an online reproduction (printed page not seen); IAEA Diagnostic Radiology Physics handbook 2014, Ch. 7 (handbook)

claims.claim: Bright light erases (the plate, before reuse)
claims.source: White & Pharoah, Oral Radiology: Principles and Interpretation, 7th ed. 2014, Ch. 4 Digital Imaging (Ludlow & Mol) - textbook, read in an online reproduction (printed page not seen); Leblans et al. 2011 (PMID 28879966), full text

claims.claim: End card. Sensor (CMOS, CCD): instant image, rigid. PSP plate: thin, film-sized, wide latitude, needs a scanner
claims.source: White & Pharoah, Oral Radiology: Principles and Interpretation, 7th ed. 2014, Ch. 4 Digital Imaging (Ludlow & Mol) - textbook, read in an online reproduction (printed page not seen) (rapid image availability, sensor bulk, film-like handling of plates); Kamburoglu et al., Imaging Sci Dent 2022;52:93-101 (PMID 35387105), PMC full text (CMOS 'bulky and rigid'); 'wide' latitude, in vitro: Berkhout et al., Dentomaxillofac Radiol 2004;33:1-5 (PMID 15140814), abstract, and Borg et al., Dentomaxillofac Radiol 2000;29:70-5 (PMID 10808218), abstract. Not claimed: 'wider than sensors' (Marinho-Vieira et al., Dentomaxillofac Radiol 2023;52:20220370, PMID 36988093, abstract)

caption:
From X-ray to pixel: a digital X-ray sensor, taken apart.
A scintillator (CsI or Gd oxysulfide) turns X-rays into light. In many sensors a fiber-optic plate carries it to the CMOS chip, where each pixel stores charge. The ADC turns charge into a number, shown as a gray level.
PSP plates trap electrons instead: red laser in, blue-violet light out, then erase with bright light. Latitude is wide, but not always wider than today's sensors.
Schematic animation.
Refs: White & Pharoah, Oral Radiology 7e (textbook); Farman 2005, OOOOE; Leblans 2011, Materials; Berkhout 2004 and Marinho-Vieira 2023, DMFR.
